A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuS-V/PULS research work. The main text, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices, including Sections 9–13, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-model evaluations, human-annotation correlations, ablations, MSR-VTT experiments and COCO-based calibration analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and reports revised model-benchmark scores for a stated 360-prompt evaluation in Table 1.

M1.justification: PULS translation, calibrated VLM perception, DTMC construction, STORM verification and ECDF scoring remain unchanged. The expanded calibration explanation and intermediate assignment in Algorithm 1 describe operations already present in v1. Replacing N with |S| in the final score expresses the average already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same four prompt themes and three complexity levels, COCO Captions calibration and MSR-VTT caption-alignment evaluation. The reported expansion from 160 to 360 prompts changes sample size without documenting a new domain, task or test scenario.

E2.justification: VBench and the GPT-4o plus LLaMa-3.2-11B or LLaVA-Video-7B alternatives remain the same comparators. The evaluated generators remain Gen-3, Pika, T2V-Turbo-v2 and CogVideoX-5B. The added original T2V-Turbo citation does not introduce another evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Table 1 report expanding the central automated benchmark from 160 to 360 prompts, while human correlations remain based on a 160-prompt subset. This substantially changes the sample basis of the model benchmarking. However, Section 13 and Table 5 retain the 160-prompt, 640-video account, leaving the additional prompts' composition and evaluation details unresolved.

E4.justification: The formal-language ablation, frame-context and VLM-choice ablations, MSR-VTT alignment test and appendix calibration analyses are retained. Their analytical questions and experimental comparisons remain unchanged; no additional robustness test or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: The Pearson-correlation reporting, correlation plots and MSR-VTT means and standard deviations remain unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests or new uncertainty-estimation procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the central benchmark's theme, complexity and overall means. Overall scores change from 0.614 to 0.723 for Gen-3, 0.409 to 0.508 for Pika, 0.417 to 0.552 for T2V-Turbo-v2 and 0.461 to 0.589 for CogVideoX-5B. These concern different reported sample sizes, so they do not establish same-setting gains. Human correlations and Tables 2–4 are unchanged. Figure 1 also changes the misaligned video's VBench score from 0.707 to 0.752.

T1.justification: v4 omits Equation (1)'s implication/eventuality consequent and closing parenthesis, leaving the displayed running-example specification incomplete; v1 contains the complete expression. This omission is visible in the rendered PDF. The accompanying interpretation, formal framework and appendix derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a formal-verification-based video metric and a temporally challenging prompt benchmark. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the over-5× human-correlation claim and the conclusion that current generators struggle with temporal fidelity.

C2.justification: Table 1's new caption asserts high correlation across all themes and complexities, extending the interpretation to every subgroup. This is overbroad given retained entries such as Gen-3's advanced-prompt correlation of -0.01. The mechanism discussion and limitation concerning unintended generated elements remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds an abstract statement announcing open-source benchmark, code and dataset access, with a project URL; v1 only promises a future release. Hardware, model settings, calibration instructions and appendix prompts remain unchanged. Future-release wording nevertheless persists elsewhere in v4.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Reward Guided Latent Consistency Distillation and the original T2V-Turbo paper, references 33–34. The related-work narrative and positioning against visual-quality and VQA-based evaluation otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording corrections, clarifies logits and calibration, makes averaging notation explicit, adds acknowledgments and replaces the repeated supplementary title with an Appendix heading. The section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves above the Methodology heading, Table 1 receives an expanded caption, and appendix prompt boxes and surrounding text shift through reflow. The same figures and tables are retained, with their overall structures largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The access link and clearer calibration and averaging explanations are useful, and the larger benchmark adds results. These benefits are outweighed by the incomplete Equation (1), unreconciled 360-versus-160-prompt reporting in the main text and appendix, and the overstated subgroup-correlation caption. With the human-validation and robustness evidence unchanged, these introduced defects produce a limited decline in mathematical clarity and reporting reliability.
